newsitem.title: USA: Cold airmass headed toward Mexican coffee regions.
newsitem.headline: Cold airmass headed toward Mexican coffee regions.

text.p: A cold airmass surging down toward Mexico will threaten the country's coffee growing regions, including major producing states Chiapas, Veracruz, Oaxaca, Puebla and Guerrero, Smith Barney meterologist Jon Davis said.
Davis said in his daily update temperatures would fall to freezing levels in Mexico later this week, which could cause some frost-related damage to the coffee trees.

"The coldest mornings will be on Thursday and Friday when lows will drop into the upper 20s F in the northern fringe of the growing area to the 30s F in the southern portion of the belt," Davis said. "These low temperatures late this week are a threat to coffee crops in parts of the belt."
Davis said while it does not look as if the cold weather will bring widespread damage, there is a potential for some damage in some sections of the Mexican coffee belt.
"Obviously, this situation needs to be watched very closely this week," he said.
By late weekend and early next week, Davis said temperatures will moderate.
